title: avoid-utf8-escape-split-and-stabilize-sse-toolcall-boundaries
author: Ethan Cole
description: Fix a class of SSE stream reassembly failures where UTF-8 escape sequences and long JSON string literals were split across transport chunks, sometimes causing partial-JSON parsing errors or mis-ordered function/tool-call sentinel emission. This change augments the chunk coalescer to treat high-risk byte sequences (UTF-8 \uXXXX escapes, JSON escape pairs like \" and \/, and CRLF boundaries) as atomic when a lookahead indicates an imminent split; it also normalizes CRLF to LF early in the framer to avoid delimiter-detection edge cases. The SSE flusher now defers emission of tool/function-call sentinel tokens until the trailing JSON fragment is fully assembled or a bounded timeout fires, preventing downstream clients from observing overlapping sentinels that led to spurious local tool invocations. The patch includes a bounded backfill heuristic (8KB cap) to fold tiny trailing fragments into the previous buffer instead of exposing partial objects to the parser, an explicit checksum sanity-check for sequence-coalescing, and conservative fallbacks for memory-constrained hosts. Test plan: add unit tests for UTF-8 escape-aware coalescing, add integration tests that simulate many CRLF and byte-level splits, and run streaming long-string regressions in CI. Rollout plan: staged canary behind feature flag, monitor streaming-parse error rate and tool-run metrics; auto-roll back on error-rate regression >3x baseline. Related: ENG-8423 (streaming robustness), ENG-8479 (openai compat toolcalling).

review_comments: Priya Nair: Could this heuristic penalize latency for very small chunks? Suggest adding a bounded lookahead so we don't stall long-tail clients. Author: Added an 8KB cap and a fallback that emits the fragment if the coalescer would exceed the cap, preserving latency for tiny payloads.

Marina Zhou: Unit tests look good but please add an integration test that simulates many small CRLF fragments and validates sentinel ordering. Author: Added the integration test and a CI rerun hook to reduce flakiness.

Lucas Kim: Why normalize CRLF at read-time vs parse-time? Author: Normalizing early simplifies downstream parsers and eliminates an entire class of off-by-one delimiter detection bugs detected during incident replay.

release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming fragmentation that could split UTF-8 escapes and JSON string fragments leading to truncated or malformed JSON events; stabilizes tool/function-call sentinel emission in OpenAI-compatible streaming clients. No public API changes. Backport recommended to release/1.3 for users on stable runtimes.
